function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

function.name: analyze_figure
function.description: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

figure_no.description: 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8.

question.description: What to ask about the figure.

force.description: 是否强制重新翻译已有译文

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

Abstract
Interactive game world models typically autoregress visual observations directly in pixel or latent space, forcing structured properties such as pose, geometry, and occlusion to be implicitly maintained by the same generative sequence. Over long horizons, errors in these latent world properties accumulate, making consistency and controllability fragile. We explicitly model the evolving world state, delegate exact geometric computation to a fixed, zero-parameter renderer, and leave the neural model to synthesize appearance. We instantiate this idea as Marionette, a world model for interactive games with articulated characters, consisting of three components. First, a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit and interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state comprising multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations. Second, a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts the predicted state into pose-control videos, computing world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form. Third, a control-conditioned video-diffusion2026 observation model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from the resulting structured controls. function.name: get_recently_submitted_cs_papers
function.description: 按 CS 子领域和最近提交时间筛选论文。按关键词、标题或作者检索时用 search_arxiv_papers。

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

save_to_file.description: true（默认）返回结果并将论文列表写入文件；false 只返回结果，不创建或写入结果文件。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

Context regimes. To evaluate the effect of the harness under different context budgets, we set a history

4.2 Main Results

Table 1 reports the full CodeSearch results. MODHARNESS-RL improves over the base harness by 19%
on average, and the gain holds at the file, module and entity level (Table 5). It also beats zero-shot
GPT-5-mini, the creator of its harness, in every setting, so the gain is not distillation from the creator.
Figure 4 applies each program alone to the base harness, and we can see that the gain from the two
programs differs by domain. On CodeSearch, STEERING improves over the base harness by 15% on
average over the four settings, which is better than COMPRESSION at 6%. On ALFWorld under a limited
budget, averaged over the two models, COMPRESSION improves by 22%, which is better than STEERING
at 16%. On BIRD SQL, the two are close with Qwen3.5-2B, and with Qwen3.5-4B, COMPRESSION performs
better.

In Figure 5, we also report the inference time, the average seconds an episode takes end to end, for
Qwen3-8B, and show that every method on the frontier is ours except INSPO under the limited budget,
which is also fast but scores below the base harness. Section 4.3 further examines these gains.

D.3 Effect of chunk length

In BAL, we set the chunk length to 4 seconds based on the definition of atomic actions in Nymeria
[25]. The chunk length controls the temporal scale represented by each latent token and is the
only hyperparameter in BAL involved in the design of the supervisory signal. Unlike augmentation
strengths or masking scales in prior methods, however, it has a direct semantic interpretation: it
specifies the temporal unit over which movement is abstracted, and can therefore be chosen intuitively
based on the expected duration of meaningful actions.
To examine how this temporal granularity affects the learned representations, we pretrain BAL
with different chunk lengths and evaluate the resulting representations on all downstream tasks. As
shown in Tab. 8, performance is consistently strong across the tested range, with every variant either
outperforming existing self-supervised methods or remaining competitive with them. Thus, BAL
achieves strong downstream performance without requiring careful tuning of the chunk length for
each task.
The results also reveal a modest dependence on the task. Shorter chunks generally perform better for
motion forecasting and interpolation, whereas longer chunks tend to benefit motion captioning. This
tendency is consistent with the nature of the downstream tasks. Because forecasting and interpolation
are evaluated directly in pose space, they benefit from fine-grained pose information, which shorter
chunks are more likely to retain. In contrast, captioning requires higher-level semantic understanding
of movements, for which longer temporal units can provide a more suitable abstraction. When further
gains are desired, the chunk length can therefore be chosen according to an intuitive notion of the
temporal granularity relevant to the target task.

F Broader impact

BAL provides a foundational framework for learning semantic representations of human movement
from 3D pose sequences, contributing to advances in human behavior modeling. These representations
may support applications involving semantic understanding of human movement, such as human-
computer interaction, assistive technologies, rehabilitation analysis, and robotics. At the same time,
improved movement representations could be misused for unauthorized surveillance or privacy-
invasive behavioral profiling, especially if applied to data collected without consent or adequate
safeguards. Although this work focuses on 3D pose sequences, similar principles may also be
explored in other sequential modalities. Applications and extensions of this work should be developed
with careful attention to consent, data privacy, fairness, and domain-specific ethical guidelines.

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

messages.content:
你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。
当前任务：获取最近14天机器学习(cs.LG)论文5篇，下载第3篇，读它的结论(conclusion)章节
我会按指定分类和时间检索论文。

A. Training details

Table 1 lists the training setup. Training runs on LIBERO (Liu et al., 2023) for 225 steps and then on two RoboDojo (Chen
et al., 2026) tasks for 115 steps (Section 4); Section 3.2 describes the RL algorithm and the training infrastructure. During
training, the framework executes the JSON object of an action as a tool call to the simulator, and the result of the call is the
next observation. The controller that executes an action is specific to each robot: it drives LIBERO’s operational-space
controller on the Franka and follows Cartesian waypoints with inverse kinematics on RoboDojo’s ARX. The reasoning
effort is xhigh in every rollout. Earlier rounds remain in the context, and an episode ends when the simulator reports success,
when the step limit or the token budget of the context is reached, or when a response contains no valid action.

Infrastructure. Our training infrastructure, PEAR (a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics), is built on veRL (Sheng
et al., 2025) and LMCache (Liu et al., 2025b). We train our models on H100, H200 and GB300 GPUs and optimize PEAR
for each of them. On H100 GPUs, we serve rollouts with tensor parallelism 4 and train the policy with FSDP (Zhao et al.,
2023) over 8 GPUs combined with 8-way sequence parallelism (Jacobs et al., 2024) (FSDP8 × SP8), so that each GPU
holds 32,512 tokens. On GB300 GPUs, we serve rollouts with tensor parallelism 2 and train the policy with FSDP4 × SP4,
with 69,632 tokens per GPU. Each node forms one FSDP group, and nodes communicate over InfiniBand. To fit such long
sequences in memory, we use gradient checkpointing (Chen et al., 2016) throughout. On H100 GPUs, we also offload
activations and use FlashAttention-3 (Shah et al., 2024), and on GB300 GPUs we use FlashAttention-4 (Zadouri et al., 2026).
Each RL step uses 128 groups of 8 rollouts. LIBERO is rendered on the CPUs of the rollout nodes, whereas RoboDojo runs
in Isaac (Mittal et al., 2025) containers on separate GPU nodes. Training took about 50,000 H100-equivalent GPU-hours in
total.

During RL on LIBERO and RoboDojo, an episode contains about 94k tokens on average (1.8k of prompt and 92k of
response), 19.7 rounds and 39 to 59 images. Episodes become shorter as training proceeds, from 119k tokens over 19.9
rounds at the start to 82k tokens over 18.5 rounds at the end. Because each round extends the same context, most of each
request is a prefix that has already been processed. On H100 nodes, LMCache offloads the KV cache of these prefixes to
CPU memory. We set the number of concurrent rollouts so that the prefix-cache hit rate stays at about 95% or above: each
engine runs 64 rollouts concurrently when sequences are capped at 160k tokens and 32 when they are capped at 256k. On
GB300 nodes, we serve without LMCache because their host memory is too small to serve as an offload tier. An H100 node
with 8 GPUs and a GB300 node with 4 GPUs each generate about 2,000 to 3,000 tokens/s during rollout. Because of some
bugs, we did not enable multi-token prediction (MTP) for rollouts, but we will support it later.

RL runs fully asynchronously in veRL, so the policy that generates a rollout lags one or two versions behind the policy
being trained. We correct for this mismatch with score centering (Marek & Ryabinin, 2026), which subtracts from each
token’s score function its expected value under the rollout policy’s next-token distribution. We use score centering alone,
without truncated importance sampling.

E. The full RoboDojo benchmark

Figure 11 shows the average success rate on the full RoboDojo simulation benchmark (Chen et al., 2026), of which
Section 4.4 reports two tasks. The benchmark has 42 tasks in five capability dimensions: Generalization, Memory, Long-
Horizon, Precision and Open. Its 12 Generalization tasks are evaluated in a standard and a randomized setting, which
gives 54 task settings, and we run 10 episodes of each, 540 episodes in total. We follow RoboDojo’s official scoring
rule: the success rate measures binary task completion, the success rate of a dimension is the mean over its tasks, and the
overall success rate is the mean of the five dimensions rather than of all tasks. The leaderboard entries of GPT-5.5 and
DeepSeek-Flash are scored with the same rule, so their results can be compared with ours.

The base model succeeds in 1 of the 540 episodes, on stack blocks random. The final model succeeds in 21 episodes:
8 of 10 on general pickup and 7 of 10 on align blocks, the two tasks used in training, and 3 of 10 on each of
match and pick from conveyor and solve equation.

A large part of the failures is due to the length of RoboDojo’s tasks. The context window of our model is 256k tokens, and
370 of the final model’s 540 episodes (68.5%) end in failure because this window is exhausted. We believe that a stronger
foundation model with a longer context window, trained with RURL, or a harness that manages the context could reach
higher success rates.

G. Real-robot trials

Table 7 lists every real-robot trial and the cause of each failure. All three models use the same protocol on the same robot at
xhigh effort, and none of them was trained on this robot or on any real-robot data. The final model was trained on the two
corresponding tasks in RoboDojo with a different robot, whereas the LIBERO-only model and the base model were not.
The final model succeeds in 18 of 30 trials, the LIBERO-only model in 7 and the base model in none. The successful trials
of the final model take between 7 and 24 rounds, and its failed trials end after between 6 and 25 rounds.

Failure causes. A trial fails when it exceeds 25 rounds or 32k reasoning tokens in a single round (Section 4), or when the
model does not complete the task. The base model runs out of rounds in 25 of its 30 trials, knocks the object over in 4 and
finishes with the blocks not aligned in 1. The 23 failures of the LIBERO-only model are more varied: it runs out of rounds
in 10 trials, knocks the object over in 4, reasons for more than 32k tokens in a single round in 4, stops automatically in an
unsafe pose in 2, does not fully lift the object in 2 and picks up the wrong object in 1. The final model shows none of these
last four kinds of failure: in its 12 failed trials, it runs out of rounds in 6, finishes with the blocks not aligned in 3 and knocks
the object over in 2, and the tennis ball rolls away in 1. No model picks up the air pump, which is knocked over in all 6 of its
trials, or the brush, with which 5 of the 6 trials run out of rounds.

H. Prompts

The system prompt consists of a protocol that is the same for every environment, an ENVIRONMENT section that is specific
to the benchmark, and the task. The template is given below, where {environment} and {instruction} stand for
the benchmark’s ENVIRONMENT section and the task instruction and all other text is given to the model as shown.

You are controlling a robot. Each turn you see the robot's current state and its camera images, and
you respond with the next action.

## OBSERVATION

The robot is made of named parts, and each part has named quantities you can set. Every turn begins
with the current value of every such quantity, grouped by part, followed by the camera images:

{"<part>": {"<quantity>": <value>, ...}, ...}

Lengths are in centimeters and angles in radians; any other quantity is a plain number. Nothing
beyond these names is given about what each quantity corresponds to.

## ACTION

The action changes the listed quantities by these amounts:

{"<part>": {"<quantity>": <change>, ...}, ...}

Write the change of every quantity; 0 leaves a quantity as it is.

## EXECUTION

The action ends once every target is reached and the robot is at rest. If something keeps a target
from being reached, the robot stops there and the action ends. Either way, you then receive the next
observation.

## RESPONSE FORMAT

End your response with exactly one fenced json block containing the action, and nothing after it:

```json
<action>
```

## ENVIRONMENT

{environment}

## TASK

{instruction}

LIBERO’s ENVIRONMENT section describes its two cameras.

−agentview: a fixed camera; the robot's base is at the top of its image, +x points toward the
bottom of the image and +y toward its left.
−wrist: a camera on the gripper; with the gripper pointing straight down at yaw 0, +x points toward
the top of its image and +y toward its right.
−the episode ends by itself as soon as the task is done: while observations keep coming, the task
is not done yet.

Robot and frame:
−left_arm and right_arm share one frame. The origin is midway between the two arms' bases, at the
height they are mounted at; +x points forward, +y to the robot's left, +z up.
−left_arm works on the +y side, right_arm on the −y side.

−Both grippers start pointing forward (roll −1.57, pitch 0, yaw 1.57).

points it straight down.
−Pointing down, yaw turns the gripper about the vertical: at yaw 1.57 its fingers sit on its left
and right and pinch along y; at yaw 0 they sit in front and behind and pinch along x.

Cameras:
−head: fixed above the robot, looking forward and down. Up in the image is +x (farther from the
robot), left is +y.
−left_wrist, right_wrist: one on each gripper, looking along its fingers, which show at the left
and right edges of the image. With the gripper pointing straight down at yaw 1.57, up in the image
is +x and left is +y.

Ending:
−The episode ends by itself as soon as the task is done: while observations keep coming, the task
is not done yet.
−Unless the task is to end up holding something, it is done only once both arms are back near the
values they started with.

−The arm's position is the point between the gripper's finger pads, about 2 above the fingertips.

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

messages.content:
你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

function.name: get_recently_submitted_cs_papers
function.description: 按 CS 子领域和最近提交时间筛选论文。按关键词、标题或作者检索时用 search_arxiv_papers。

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

messages.content:
你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。
接下来使用指定引用 1。我会提交翻译任务。
{"task_id": "mocktask0001", "paper_id": "2608.14539v1", "status": "PENDING"}

function.name: get_recently_submitted_cs_papers
function.description: 按 CS 子领域和最近提交时间筛选论文。按关键词、标题或作者检索时用 search_arxiv_papers。

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

save_to_file.description: true（默认）返回结果并将论文列表写入文件；false 只返回结果，不创建或写入结果文件。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

function.name: get_paper_content
function.description: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

function.name: summarize_paper
function.description: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

max_words.description: Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250.

function.name: extract_paper_figures
function.description: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

function.name: analyze_figure
function.description: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

figure_no.description: 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8.

question.description: What to ask about the figure.

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

当前任务：只检查第1篇论文的缓存状态，不要下载或翻译

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers：{"paper_count": 5, "papers": [{"ref": 1, "paper_id": "2608.14539v1", "title": "Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils"}, {"ref": 2, "paper_id": "2608.14530v1", "title": "Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance"}, {"ref": 3, "paper_id": "2608.14528v1", "title": "Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries"}, {"ref": 4, "paper_id": "2611.18553v1", "title": "WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers"}, {"ref": 5, "paper_id": "2611.18543v1", "title": "Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning"}]}
- 当前候选列表有 5 篇。
- 当前没有最近操作的论文。
接下来使用指定引用 1。我会查询缓存状态。
{"paper_id": "2608.14539v1", "pdf": null, "translate": null, "pdf_ready": false, "translated_ready": false}
2608.14539v1 的 PDF 未就绪，译文未就绪。

function.name: get_recently_submitted_cs_papers
function.description: 按 CS 子领域和最近提交时间筛选论文。按关键词、标题或作者检索时用 search_arxiv_papers。

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

save_to_file.description: true（默认）返回结果并将论文列表写入文件；false 只返回结果，不创建或写入结果文件。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

function.name: get_paper_content
function.description: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

function.name: summarize_paper
function.description: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

max_words.description: Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250.

function.name: extract_paper_figures
function.description: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

function.name: analyze_figure
function.description: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

figure_no.description: 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8.

question.description: What to ask about the figure.

function.name: translate_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 提交 PDF 全文翻译。PENDING 表示已受理，译文尚未就绪，请勿重提交或轮询。用户明确要求时可随后查询一次缓存。默认只保留中文单语 PDF。

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新翻译已有译文

function.name: get_paper_cache_status
function.description: 只查询 PDF 下载状态和中文译文就绪状态，不发起下载或翻译。用户要求先下载再检查时，先调用下载工具再查询。提交翻译后可按用户要求查询一次，PENDING 不代表译文可读。

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

function.name: get_translated_content
function.description: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

page.description: 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract.

2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

function.description: 按 CS 子领域和最近提交时间筛选论文。按关键词、标题或作者检索时用 search_arxiv_papers。

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

save_to_file.description: true（默认）返回结果并将论文列表写入文件；false 只返回结果，不创建或写入结果文件。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

function.name: get_paper_content
function.description: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

function.name: summarize_paper
function.description: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.

max_words.description: Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250.

你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

Abstract
Determining the biological sex of the individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils remains a chal-
lenging problem due to the absence of ground truth, population differences between contemporary and pre-
historic groups, and the uncertainty introduced by image degradation. Traditional morphometric methods
suffer from high structural overlap across sexes, poor cross-population generalizability, and subjective feature2026 engineering. This study presents an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework for sex attribution in prehis-
toric hand stencils that explicitly models, propagates, and aggregates uncertainty throughout the analytical
pipeline. The methodology combines dual image processing, dual contour extraction, structured silhouetteAug augmentation, model architectural diversity, and ensemble-based decision aggregation. The pipeline generates
twelve plausible silhouette realizations per stencil to capture boundary uncertainties, which are processed by14
two ensembles of ten deep neural networks each (EfficientNet-B3 and MobileViT-S) trained on 14,036 con-
temporary hand samples. Furthermore, a triangulated validation scheme integrates ensemble predictions with
unsupervised 2D latent-space manifold mapping (UMAP + k-NN) and explainable AI spatial attributions
(LayerCAM) to ensure anatomical consistency. On contemporary data, ensemble models achieve strong classi-
fication performance, with accuracies exceeding 88% in older age groups. When applied to prehistoric stencils,[cs.CV]the framework produces both sex predictions and confidence measures of internal agreement, enabling the
distinction between morphologically stable and ambiguous cases. The convergence observed across ensemble
predictions, latent-space structure, and interpretability analyses suggests that uncertainty can be transformed
into an explicit and measurable component of archaeological inference, providing a robust, transparent, and
reproducible approach to decoding ancient rock art.

Keywords: Prehistoric hand stencils, hand silhouettes, sex classification, deep learning, uncertainty
management, explainable AI

标题和摘要。
Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils

Abstract
Determining the biological sex of the individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils remains a chal-
lenging problem due to the absence of ground truth, population differences between contemporary and pre-
historic groups, and the uncertainty introduced by image degradation. Traditional morphometric methods
suffer from high structural overlap across sexes, poor cross-population generalizability, and subjective feature2026 engineering. This study presents an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework for sex attribution in prehis-
toric hand stencils that explicitly models, propagates, and aggregates uncertainty throughout the analytical
pipeline. The methodology combines dual image processing, dual contour extraction, structured silhouetteAug augmentation, model architectural diversity, and ensemble-based decision aggregation. The pipeline generates
twelve plausible silhouette realizations per stencil to capture boundary uncertainties, which are processed by14
two ensembles of ten deep neural networks each (EfficientNet-B3 and MobileViT-S) trained on 14,036 con-
temporary hand samples. Furthermore, a triangulated validation scheme integrates ensemble predictions with
unsupervised 2D latent-space manifold mapping (UMAP + k-NN) and explainable AI spat

标题和摘要。
Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries

Abstract
AbstractAug This study investigates the methodological and theoretical properties of session 14 handover in applications that use large language models. A task may continue in a new session when the context reaches the model’s input limit, when the application restarts, or when another agent is asked to finish the task. The application must then decide which information from the earlier session to pass on. aspect.description: * 表示全部计算机科学子领域。AI、CV、RO、CL、LG、CR 等为类别短码，cs.CV 对应 CV。

days.description: 查询最近多少天的论文

output_path.description: 保存搜索结果的路径。save_to_file=true 时，null 或空路径使用默认路径。save_to_file=false 时忽略此项，使用 null 或省略。

function.name: search_arxiv_papers
function.description: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文。仅按 cs.CV 等类别筛选时用 get_recently_submitted_cs_papers。

query.description: 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段

days.description: 只检索最近多少天内提交的论文；null 表示不限制时间。

function.name: download_arxiv_pdf
function.description: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

force.description: 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）

function.name: get_paper_content
function.description: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.

ref.description: 当前会话候选列表的 1-based 序号、完整 arXiv ID（保留版本后缀）或标题片段。省略或 null 指最近操作的论文；没有最近操作对象时无法解析。

section.description: Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract.

function.name: summarize_paper

messages.content:
你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

近年来，图像生成技术取得了显著进展[2, 5, 15, 17, 19]。顶级闭源模型（如 GPT-Image2[13]、Nano Banan
a Pro[3]）现在具备在交错的图像-文本复杂指令指导下执行复杂图像编辑的能力。图像编辑模型的应用场
景正在快速从简单试验转向实际部署，用户越来越渴望将这些模型直接整合到实际生产环境中。然而，

to global position and heading. It also makes the state render-ready, since a fixed operator can reconstruct
metric world-space joints from s (§3.3). The control signal ct carries, per entity, a discrete action id from
an action vocabulary, naming what the character is doing (attacking, dodging, walking), and the character
heading; the root displacement and rotation can be overwritten the same way (Appendix D). All of it enters
the dynamics model.

Three components then realize Eq. 1. A dynamics model p(st+1: | s≤t, c) predicts future states (§3.2), a
deterministic render operator R(s) produces a pose-control video (§3.3), and an observation model p(obs |
R(s)) synthesizes RGB (§3.4). The offloading principle fixes where the cut falls. Metric geometry, root
integration, joint kinematics, and camera projection are all computed by the zero-parameter operator R, and
the neural models are responsible only for plausible dynamics and appearance.

3.2 Two-stage dynamics: decision then animation

The dynamics model factors the next-state prediction into a discrete decision stage and a continuous animation
stage. This is a small instance of the decoupling principle. The decision of what to do is discrete and
low-dimensional; the body motion that carries it out is continuous and high-dimensional.

ActionGPT (decision). A compact causal transformer (4 layers, width 256, ∼2.5M parameters) autoregresses
one discrete action token per frame per entity, drawn from that entity’s action vocabulary. It is conditioned
on a low-dimensional summary of recent state: the 18D root/rotation stream, learned action embeddings,
animation progress, and the weapon sub-state. It additionally regresses the next root motion and orientation.
Because the action is an explicit token, control is applied by overwriting that token. To make a character
perform a desired action we override the sampled token with the target action id at that frame, with no
retraining and no auxiliary conditioning network. A player’s button press would enter the model at exactly

this point, which is also where our scripted control experiments inject their commands; §4.3 shows that the
forced token has causal authority over the resulting pose.

PoseGPT (animation). A larger causal transformer (8 layers, width 512, ∼25M parameters) maps the chosen
action tokens and recent body state to the next-frame 258D body pose (the two entities’ relative joint
positions and the weapon). It acts as an animation player, mapping the chosen action to the resulting body
configuration. This split keeps the control interface compact and interpretable, while pose synthesis gets
the capacity it needs.

Autoregressive rollout. At each step ActionGPT proposes actions and root motion, and an optional control
override replaces the action tokens. PoseGPT animates the body for those actions, the two are assembled into
the next 276D state, and the state is appended to the context. The loop repeats within a bounded attention
window. Optional terrain conditioning, in the form of an egocentric height patch and per-joint ground
clearances encoded by a small MLP, feeds both stages, and the animation stage carries ground-contact and
non-penetration objectives so that the predicted motion respects the local ground surface.

3.3 Deterministic graphics bridge

The bridge R turns a state sequence into a pose-control video with zero learnable parameters. For each frame
it converts the 6D root rotations [97] to rotation matrices by Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization, then rotates
each per-frame root delta into the world frame and integrates it by cumulative sum to recover the absolute
root trajectory. It places every relative joint by adding the root-frame-rotated offsets to the root position,
which yields metric world-space skeletons for both entities. It then views the scene with a camera, by
default a deterministic follow-camera that frames the two entities, or a supplied ground-truth view for
evaluation, and rasterizes the skeletons into the pose-control frame the observation model consumes.

Every step here is a closed-form geometric operation, so world-space consistency, correct occlusion ordering,
and metric scale hold by construction. The rendered geometry can drift only if the predicted state drifts,
which is what the state-layer metrics measure.

The bridge also carries the scanned terrain, the one part of the world that neither recorded view contains
and that both the renderer and the dynamics model consume. The state is metric and open to inspection,
so the bridge can enforce feasibility rather than encourage it, by projecting an infeasible root back onto the
ground surface at the frame it appears. The pose-control frame is built as a three-channel geometry buffer,
packing height, per-joint identity, and inverse depth into channels the observation model can read back.
Appendix C gives the encoding, the terrain representation, and the effect of both on the training objective
and on inference. Figure 2 shows the bridge on a real rollout: the rasterized pose-control frames (top) and
the RGB frames the observation model renders from them (bottom), frame-aligned over twelve seconds.

The observation model is a control-conditioned video-diffusion model (Wan2.2-Fun-5B) built on a modern
DiT video backbone [48, 65], of the family that also underlies recent large video generators [33, 76]. It maps

single diffusion window we use a chunk-relay rollout, in the spirit of autoregressive long-video generation
[79, 38]: the model generates a fixed-length chunk and its final frames seed the next one. Appearance is
propagated this way, while the underlying geometry and dynamics stay governed by the explicit state and
the deterministic bridge. Because the diffusion model handles appearance only, long-horizon geometric
consistency depends on the state layer, and appearance consistency remains its own (§5)."}

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

• [构建全面任务覆盖系统，填补多图像评估空白。] 我们提出了 CPI-General-Bench，其通用子集涵盖了
30 个广泛且多样的编辑任务。关键是，通过引入 10 个多图像编辑任务，我们解决了现有基准测试中
长期以来对多图像交互能力的忽视，为评估复杂推理和一致性维护提供了标准化测试平台。

• [为真实世界消费者场景开创面向部署的基准测试。] 我们推出了CPI-Practical-Benchmark，一个关注实

• [图像编辑模型的全方位评估] CPI-Bench 提供了对图像编辑模型在三个关键维度上的整体性能评估：通
用编辑能力、实际部署效能以及模型智能水平。

• [揭示复杂场景中的真实性能差距。] 实验证明，CPI-Bench 有效突破了现有基准测试仅限于简单单图任
务的“性能饱和”瓶颈。在 CPI-Bench 上，不同模型之间的性能差异显著增强，清晰地刻画了模型在
处理高要求推理指令、多图像关联及实际应用中的能力层级，从而指出了下一代图像编辑模型迭代优
化的关键路径。

• [通过竞技场相关性与人类偏好对齐] 我们的排序分析显示，在所有评估的基准中，CPI-Bench 与竞技场
图像编辑排行榜的统计对齐度最高。这种强相关性证明，CPI-Bench 不仅仅测量技术指标，而是忠实
反映了人类评估者的感知判断和偏好。因此，它作为一种稳健、可靠的现实用户体验代理，可以确保
模型优化由真实的人类需求驱动，而非人为的基准伪影。

2 相关工作

2.1 图像编辑基准
尽管被广泛使用，现有的通用基准[11, 21, 27]仍然受到任务覆盖范围狭窄和主要关注单图像设置的限制。
它们的分类法在很大程度上依赖抽象能力维度，常常忽视实际部署的细微差别。最重要的是，这些基准
完全忽略了多图像编辑这一关键领域。

此外，现有的一般图像编辑基准缺乏基于推理的评估数据，使其无法评估编辑模型的智能水平。相反，
当前的推理特定基准在认知能力的关注上过于单一，并且在范围上存在明显的局限性：RISEBench [29]
主要评估时间、因果、空间和逻辑维度；KRIS-Bench [26] 引入了一个涵盖事实、概念和过程类型的知识

你是一个 arXiv 计算机科学论文研究助手。

根据用户目标和当前会话状态使用工具。每轮最多调用一个工具。优先利用已有会话上下文和历史结果。

调用工具前可以用一句简短自然的话说明已知状态和下一步动作。以用户请求、会话状态和工具结果为依据。不要输出冗长的内部推理或隐藏思考标签。

工具名称、参数含义、类型、合法取值和默认行为以工具定义为准。只调用提供的工具。

### 用户约束与任务完成规则

1. 遵守用户约束：用户明确提出的禁止条件、范围限制、参数要求和步骤顺序必须遵守。工具默认行为与用户限制冲突时，选择能够满足限制的合法参数；只执行与用户目标相关的操作。
2. 跟踪任务进度：根据用户请求、历史交互和真实工具 Observation，判断已完成、待完成和受阻的步骤。按用户要求及步骤依赖继续执行；只有全部必需步骤完成或存在明确阻塞时，才能给出最终回答。区分 PENDING 和 READY，不重复提交或无意义轮询。若用户要求且后续步骤不依赖待就绪的结果，继续执行；若依赖该结果，说明尚未就绪。
3. 处理阻塞与部分完成：缺少必要上下文、引用无效或工具能力不支持时，说明具体原因，不猜测或编造。若其他独立子目标仍可执行且不违反用户约束，应继续完成，并分别汇报完成情况和阻塞原因。工具出错后，根据错误修正可修正的调用，不原样重试。

最终回答直接交付用户要求的结果和必要状态。每个结果汇报一次，回答完即结束。

{"paper_id": "2608.14530v1", "title": "Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance", "section": "method", "content": "3.1 Problem formulation

We represent the world by an explicit, interpretable state st ∈R276 that describes the physical configuration
of the scene at frame t. For each of the two articulated entities, a monster M and a player character
(the hunter) N, it holds a per-frame root displacement, joint positions relative to that root, and the root
orientation as a continuous 6D rotation, together with a small weapon sub-state:

s = [ δM0:3 , pM3:162 , δN162:165 , pN165:258 , w258:264 , rM264:270 , rN270:276 ].
|{z}root 53×3| {zjoints} | root{z } 31×3| {zjoints} |weapon{z } |6D{zrot} |6D{zrot}

Storing joints relative to the root, and root motion as a per-frame delta, makes the representation invariant
to global position and heading. It also makes the state render-ready, since a fixed operator can reconstruct
metric world-space joints from s (§3.3). The control signal ct carries, per entity, a discrete action id from
an action vocabulary, naming what the character is doing (attacking, dodging, walking), and the character
heading; the root displacement and rotation can be overwritten the same way (Appendix D). All of it enters
the dynamics model.

Three components then realize Eq. 1. A dynamics model p(st+1: | s≤t, c) predicts future states (§3.2), a
deterministic render operator R(s) produces a pose-control video (§3.3), and an observation model p(obs |
R(s)) synthesizes RGB (§3.4). The offloading principle fixes where the cut falls. Metric geometry, root
integration, joint kinematics, and camera projection are all computed by the zero-parameter operator R, and
the neural models are responsible only for plausible dynamics and appearance.

3.2 Two-stage dynamics: decision then animation

The dynamics model factors the next-state prediction into a discrete decision stage and a continuous animation
stage. This is a small instance of the decoupling principle. The decision of what to do is discrete and
low-dimensional; the body motion that carries it out is continuous and high-dimensional.

ActionGPT (decision). A compact causal transformer (4 layers, width 256, ∼2.5M parameters) autoregresses
one discrete action token per frame per entity, drawn from that entity’s action vocabulary. It is conditioned
on a low-dimensional summary of recent state: the 18D root/rotation stream, learned action embeddings,
animation progress, and the weapon sub-state. It additionally regresses the next root motion and orientation.
Because the action is an explicit token, control is applied by overwriting that token. To make a character
perform a desired action we override the sampled token with the target action id at that frame, with no
retraining and no auxiliary conditioning network. A player’s button press would enter the model at exactly

4

pose-control video (deterministic bridge)

rendered RGB (observation model)

Figure 2 The deterministic bridge on a 12-second generated rollout. Top: pose-control frames rasterized from the
predicted state (terrain depth encoding with both entities’ skeletons). Bottom: the RGB frames the observation model
renders from them. The geometry shared by the two rows is computed by the bridge, not generated by a neural model.

this point, which is also where our scripted control experiments inject their commands; §4.3 shows that the
forced token has causal authority over the resulting pose.

PoseGPT (animation). A larger causal transformer (8 layers, width 512, ∼25M parameters) maps the chosen
action tokens and recent body state to the next-frame 258D body pose (the two entities’ relative joint
positions and the weapon). It acts as an animation player, mapping the chosen action to the resulting body
configuration. This split keeps the control interface compact and interpretable, while pose synthesis gets
the capacity it needs.

Autoregressive rollout. At each step ActionGPT proposes actions and root motion, and an optional control
override replaces the action tokens. PoseGPT animates the body for those actions, the two are assembled into
the next 276D state, and the state is appended to the context. The loop repeats within a bounded attention
window. Optional terrain conditioning, in the form of an egocentric height patch and per-joint ground
clearances encoded by a small MLP, feeds both stages, and the animation stage carries ground-contact and
non-penetration objectives so that the predicted motion respects the local ground surface.

3.3 Deterministic graphics bridge

The bridge R turns a state sequence into a pose-control video with zero learnable parameters. For each frame
it converts the 6D root rotations [97] to rotation matrices by Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization, then rotates
each per-frame root delta into the world frame and integrates it by cumulative sum to recover the absolute
root trajectory. It places every relative joint by adding the root-frame-rotated offsets to the root position,
which yields metric world-space skeletons for both entities. It then views the scene with a camera, by
default a deterministic follow-camera that frames the two entities, or a supplied ground-truth view for
evaluation, and rasterizes the skeletons into the pose-control frame the observation model consumes.

Every step here is a closed-form geometric operation, so world-space consistency, correct occlusion ordering,
and metric scale hold by construction. The rendered geometry can drift only if the predicted state drifts,
which is what the state-layer metrics measure.

The bridge also carries the scanned terrain, the one part of the world that neither recorded view contains
and that both the renderer and the dynamics model consume. The state is metric and open to inspection,
so the bridge can enforce feasibility rather than encourage it, by projecting an infeasible root back onto the
ground surface at the frame it appears. The pose-control frame is built as a three-channel geometry buffer,
packing height, per-joint identity, and inverse depth into channels the observation model can read back.
Appendix C gives the encoding, the terrain representation, and the effect of both on the training objective
and on inference. Figure 2 shows the bridge on a real rollout: the rasterized pose-control frames (top) and
the RGB frames the observation model renders from them (bottom), frame-aligned over twelve seconds.

5
3.4 Observation model and long-horizon rollout

The observation model is a control-conditioned video-diffusion model (Wan2.2-Fun-5B) built on a modern
DiT video backbone [48, 65], of the family that also underlies recent large video generators [33, 76]. It maps
the pose-control video from R, together with a first-frame image for identity/appearance, to photorealistic
RGB. For entities carried in the state it does not need to infer geometry, and the one long-range quantity it
still carries is appearance identity across chunks (§5). Its job is to render the geometry it is given, which
is the regime in which pose-guided video synthesis is strong [27, 99, 89]. For horizons far beyond a
single diffusion window we use a chunk-relay rollout, in the spirit of autoregressive long-video generation
[79, 38]: the model generates a fixed-length chunk and its final frames seed the next one. Appearance is
propagated this way, while the underlying geometry and dynamics stay governed by the explicit state and
the deterministic bridge. Because the diffusion model handles appearance only, long-horizon geometric
consistency depends on the state layer, and appearance consistency remains its own (§5)."}
